Raj: FYI — after the token-budget tweak at 10:03 UTC p99 latency for small chat reqs (<=32 tokens) spiked. p99 went ~80ms -> ~320ms
Sophia: seeing the same in synthetic replay. small-shape throughput down ~18% :eyes:
Oliver: can you paste the timeline + any quick profiler traces? any kernel flips or KV thrash?
Raj: dropping a trimmed runtime snippet below:
Raj: ```
2026-03-15T10:03:12Z INFO continuous-batcher: token_budget_target=12 -> 6
2026-03-15T10:03:12Z INFO batcher: window_ms=15 -> 7
2026-03-15T10:04:02Z WARN batch-assembly: microbatch_stutter id=0x9a3 cnt=5 observed_ms=260
2026-03-15T10:04:02Z INFO kernel-selection: selected_kernel=gemm_int8_affine alt_kernel=fused_attention table_bucket=small_col
2026-03-15T10:04:02Z WARN kv-cache: eviction_rate=140/s prefix_hit=0.39
```
Ken: looks like the selector is switching to an int8 GEMM path a lot. That helps big batches but on tiny microbatches the per-kernel enqueue cost dominates and you see driver queue gaps.
Sophia: I ran a quick inline profiler on a repro trace; results show kernel enqueue lag is the biggest contributor:
Sophia: ```
metrics:
  batch_assembly_ms: 42
  kv_fetch_ms: 7
  kernel_enqueue_ms: 118
  kernel_exec_ms: 36
  post_process_ms: 10
```
Maria: the KV eviction spike makes sense — smaller budgets -> more fragmented prefixes -> less reuse -> more evictions + cache churn.
Raj: is kernel_enqueue coming from CPU scheduling saturation or the GPU driver queue? the nvtx trace I saw had long pending gaps.
Ken: it's the driver-side per-kernel overhead on our Ampere racks. When we fragment into many short kernels (gemm fragments) enqueue overhead shows up as ~100ms gaps. The token_budget tweak increased microbatch count which exacerbates this.
Oliver: I reproduced locally with a small-shape workload. token_budget=6 yields ~3-4x microbatch ops and kernel_selector sometimes chooses a different kernel bucket for those shapes.
Sophia: nvtx capture shows intermittent "pending" states ~90-130ms between enqueue and start. That lines up with kernel_enqueue_ms.
Maria: mitigation idea: raise token_budget modestly for small-shape traffic (e.g., to 10), and add a tiny coalesce window to let microbatches join. That should reduce per-kernel enqueue count.
Raj: another option is to bias kernel_selector to prefer fused_attention or fused_fwd kernel for microbatches <=4, which reduces fragmentation of work.
Ken: propose a canary: runtime flags --batch-assembly-coalesce-ms=3 and kernel_selector.debug=1 on a small rack. If we see p99 drop without hurting big-shape throughput we can roll the heuristic tweak instead of full rollback.
Oliver: starting canary on r3a-50 now and will run replay.
deploy-bot: deploy started r3a-50 canary with flags: --batch-assembly-coalesce-ms=3 kernel_selector.debug=1 (commit abc1234)
Sophia: replay running — first 3 minutes look better. p99 down from ~320ms -> ~110ms (baseline ~82ms). Still above baseline but much improved.
Maria: kv eviction on canary dropped to ~30/s, prefix_hit=0.79 :thumbsup:
Ken: seems like the right hybrid: slightly higher token_budget for small class + small coalesce window + selector bias for tiny shapes.
Raj: next steps: 1) let canary run 30m and collect nvtx + kernel enqueue histograms; 2) Ken to prepare selector-rule PR for fused-kernel bias; 3) consider per-traffic-class token_budget (we already tag traffic) and add regression test to perf suite.
Oliver: added a short deterministic perf test that reproduces the stutter, PR coming (link: github.com/redwood-infer/perf/PR-122)
Sophia: logging tweak: emit `batch_assembly.reason` and `kernel_selector.decision` with IDs for a few hours to correlate metrics with traces.
Maria: I'll add a metric alarm: kv_cache.eviction_rate > 50/s for small-shape tag triggers paging and an oncall notify.
Raj: thanks all. If canary stabilizes we'll ship targeted heuristic change instead of rolling back the broader token-budget update. Keep posting nvtx snippets and the kernel_selector debug logs here. :metal:
